To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synthetic peptide vaccines, which are immunogenic in mice and humans, can be used to inhibit the growth and metastatic spread of human breast tumors.
immunization of mice with synthetic peptides related to a human breast tumor-associated mucin (MUC1), using a variety of immunization protocols, induced both specific IgG and DTH responses.
synthetic peptides that are related to the core sequence of the tandem repeat encoded by the human breast mucin gene can be used to elicit a strong antibody and cell-mediated immune response in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a peptide vaccine against breast cancer.
the development of immunotherapeutic agents based on the MUC1 mucins that are overexpressed by the majority of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and colon cancers.
the immunobiology of the MUCI mucin molecule and its role in the development and progression of human breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MUC1 core peptide is immunogenic in mice and that the MUC-1 core peptide can be used as an immunogen to induce a protective immune response in mice.
the immunogenicity of the MUC 1 synthetic peptide vaccines is dependent on the immunization protocol and on the type of molecule used.

immunization with synthetic peptides, either as SP-KLH or SP-MAP-4 molecules, induces a specific immune response that can be used to inhibit the growth and metastasis of human breast cancer cells that express the human MUC-1 mucin gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immunization of CAF1 and BALB/c mice with various MUC1 synthetic peptide vaccines, including SP-KLH and SP — MAP- 4, induced specific IgG, IgG1 and IgG2a antibodies that recognized the appropriate peptides, and bound the cell surface expressed human MUC1 on MUC1-trans-fected cells.
the immunogenicity of MUC1 synthetic peptide “vaccinations” is dependent on the immunization protocol and the nature of the synthetic peptide.

synthetic peptides, which are related to a MUC1 muc1 epitope, can be used to immunize mice and that the resulting immune response may be useful in inhibiting the growth of Muc1 expressing tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synthetic peptides can induce both humoral and cellular immune responses to MUC1.
the synthetic peptides related to MUC1 can be used as immunogens for inducing a strong immune response in mice, and that this immune response can be used for the prevention of MUC1 expressing tumors.
the MUC1 peptide epitopes are immunogenic in the mouse model.
